FACTORY GOAL
Build the strongest specification-faithful Pocketful service possible through Stage 4, while preserving genuine Band teamwork evidence and a reusable, generic factory. Optimize for correctness and judgeability, not for chat volume.

TEAM ROLES
@arulmuruganmuthuvel29/pocketfullead = coordinator/architect/integration owner

IMPORTANT: every handoff must mention the recipient by literal @handle and contain the complete task plus relevant specification requirements. Do not make recipients infer the task from room history.

PARALLEL EXECUTION
Run independent discovery and review work in parallel. Do NOT let two agents modify the same product source files at the same time. The Builder owns source-code integration; specialist seats may create disjoint regression tests, audit notes, or packaging docs, then hand findings to the Builder. The Lead controls merge/integration order.

PACKAGE 1 — ARCHITECT / REQUIREMENTS
Read the participant guide and all four Pocketful specs completely. Build a requirement/invariant matrix and stage dependency map. Identify exact status/error precedence, boundary-time semantics, idempotency semantics, concurrency/atomicity constraints, cumulative-stage rules, deployment contract, generic-mandate rules, roster/room evidence requirements and final submission gates. Send the COMPLETE Stage 1 handoff to @[[2bcaaa4a-ca1e-493d-b7b0-edba8a182cd2]] and explicit review tasks to the specialists.

PACKAGE 2 — STAGE 1
Implement Stage 1 in stage-1/ from the official specification, not from tests. Cover auth, passwords, tokens, handles, exact integer money and integral JSON handling, timestamps, payments, requests, visibility, required idempotency semantics including concurrent retries, split arithmetic/remainder ordering and settlements/aggregate affordability/atomicity, export/import and exact errors. Build Dockerfile and RUN.md. Run the shipped tests plus project-owned adversarial tests. Stage 1 must be a standalone complete buildable service.

PACKAGE 3 — STAGE 2
After Stage 1 is accepted, copy stage-1/ to stage-2/ and extend it to the complete Stage 2 specification. Cover browser UI, required DOM/test hooks, stale state, lost-response/retry recovery, authorizations, holds, partial/final capture, void, expiry and exact total/available/held semantics. Run real browser checks. Do not copy later-stage surfaces backward into stage-1.

PACKAGE 4 — STAGE 3
After Stage 2 is accepted, copy stage-2/ to stage-3/ and extend it to the Stage 3 specification. Cover immutable revisions, effective_at vs recorded_at, as_of/known_at, historical balances and holds/releases, half-open statement ranges, stable ordering, pagination, snapshot stability, corrections, stale revisions and historical overdraft prevention. Attack concurrent/history boundary cases.

PACKAGE 5 — STAGE 4
After Stage 3 is accepted, copy stage-3/ to stage-4/ and extend it to Stage 4. Cover receiver refunds, cumulative refund ceilings, target/refund immutability, correction/refund interaction, settlement correction batches 1..32, completeness, identical effective time where required, aggregate/historical affordability, atomic rejection, shared recorded_at/batch id, replay/idempotency and exact precedence.

PACKAGE 6 — RED TEAM
Independently attack each accepted stage. Focus on the hidden behaviors that shipped tests cannot cover: lost response then retry, concurrent same-key writes, same key across body/path/method, failed-key reuse, malformed JSON types, exact timestamp boundaries, concurrent balance races, statement snapshot races, historical known_at/as_of combinations, hold-expiry/capture/void races, refund/correction ordering, incomplete settlement correction batches, import/export fidelity and stage gating. Reject only with reproducible evidence and send exact evidence to the owning seat.

PACKAGE 7 — UI / RELEASE
Inspect every stage for browser correctness, visible errors, stale state, retry/recovery, accessibility/basic usability, data-testid contract and route reachability. Separately audit Dockerfiles, RUN.md, generic mandates, README.md, FACTORY.md, secrets, databases, logs, pycache, nested .git, symlinks/submodules and reproducibility. Generic mandates MUST NOT name track-specific endpoints, fields, error codes or test ids.

PACKAGE 8 — FINAL VERIFY
@[[06d46baf-53d9-4b9e-84e4-535963463b73]] is an independent release gate. Re-run the strongest official harness available against the committed final revision. Run every contiguous stage from 1 upward. Verify the service in clean containers, clean-clone mode, and run git diff --check plus secret scanning. Verify exact pass/fail/error counts. Do not self-certify findings from the verifier's own prior work.

STAGE GATING
Use ONE result repository and ONE Band room. Stage folders are cumulative. A stage may claim only its own requirements. Do not put the final Stage 4 answer into earlier folders. Every stage folder must build and start independently. A later-stage feature must not leak into earlier stage behavior.

TEST DISCIPLINE
Never modify the official tests. Never hard-code hidden answers. Never write code only to satisfy visible tests. Build to the written specification and use project-owned tests only as supplemental evidence.

SELF-DOUBT / TOP-QUALITY REVIEW
At every stage gate, each reviewer must ask:
- What hidden test would most likely break this?
- Which requirement is easiest to misread?
- What happens under concurrent retry?
- What happens exactly at the boundary?
- What happens after a lost response?
- What happens if state changes between requests?
- What happens if one batch item is invalid?
- What happens when current and historical views differ?
- What happens when refund and correction interact?
- What happens in a clean environment?
Turn important doubts into executable tests.

FINAL DRAWBACK ROUND

{"is_error":false,"name":"Bash","output":"# Pocketful — Stage 1: payments and settlements

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.

## 1. Scope

Users can send money by handle, request money and split bills. Payments appear in an
activity feed with public or private visibility. Authorized operators can submit groups
of transfers as settlements. Only the HTTP API is required.

The following apply to all operations, including concurrent requests and retries:

1. The sum of wallet balances always equals the total seeded by the last `POST /_test/reset`.
2. No wallet balance may be negative, including transiently.
3. A payment request may move money at most once.

All amounts are exact integer counts of minor units. Deposits, top-ups, withdrawals,
cards and bank integrations are out of scope. Money moves only between existing wallets.
